title: [Audit 1.1] One intake service for single, batch and walk-in intake
body:
Part of the 2026-10 LIMS audit plan, **Phase 1: Write paths, state machine, identifiers**, item **1.1**. Tracking issue: #162

Audited at `main` @ `477cc1f`. Paths given as a bare file name live under `server/controllers/`, `server/services/`, `server/utils/`, `server/routes/` or `client/src/components/...`. Line numbers may have moved; if a line doesn't match, search for the quoted symbol and confirm the problem still exists before changing anything.

## Problem (audit findings)

- **A3** (P1): Acceptance can bypass the compliance checklist, mass and custody checks. Two routes do this:
  • `/receive` → `/accept`
  • generic `PUT /:id/status` to `ACCEPTED`, gated by `APPROVE_RESULTS` (not a reception permission). It generates a Lab ID before the transaction
  - Evidence: `sampleController.js:791,1377,432-441,501-537`
- **A5** (P1): Work items and the order revision are generated outside the intake transaction. Failures are only logged. There is no unique (sampleId, analysis), so duplicate items are possible
  - Evidence: `receptionController.js:1104-1110`; `sampleController.js:523-530`; `workItemController.js:83-100,140-165,220`
- **A8** (P1): Batch intake has its own copy of work-item creation. It lacks:
  • code normalisation
  • methodology defaults
  • OrderRevision
  • per-sample audit
  • checklist evaluation
  - Evidence: `receptionController.js:2079-2120,2155,395`
- **A13** (P1): Intake creates the sample before validating, so failed attempts leave orphan EXPECTED samples. A missing originalId becomes the string `"undefined"`
  - Evidence: `receptionController.js:464,483,755,812,842`
- **A22** (P2): Consignment code is `count+1` computed outside the transaction, so collisions return 500. `expectedCount` defaults to the received count, which hides discrepancies
  - Evidence: `receptionController.js:1821,1831,1927`; `BatchIntake.jsx:176`

## Change to make

- Change: create `server/services/intakeService.js` with `acceptSample(tx, input)` and `rejectSample(tx, input)`. Use it from single intake, batch intake, walk-in and Kobo-confirmed arrival. In one transaction it:
  1. validates (checklist, mass vs `sampleMassRequired` sum, custody, catalogue)
  2. creates or updates the sample
  3. allocates the lab sample code (1.3)
  4. transitions through `transitionSample`
  5. creates gates + WorkItems + OrderRevision v1 + OrderLines (normalised codes)
  6. writes the audit rows
  - Validation runs before anything is created.
  - Remove `/receive` + `/accept`, or route them through the service.
  - Generic `PUT /:id/status` can no longer target ACCEPTED.
- Data model: `@@unique([sampleId, analysis])` on WorkItem, which needs a dedupe migration script first. List the duplicates; do not auto-delete ones that have results.
- Acceptance:
  - [test] Injected failure in work-item creation → no sample is ACCEPTED (rollback).
  - [test] A failed validation creates no sample.
  - [test] Batch and single intake produce identical WorkItems, OrderLines and audit rows for the same input.

## Edge cases to handle

- Kobo-confirmed arrivals with an open provenance hold are refused (until 1.6 they use the existing metadata check).
- Re-intake of a RECEIVED_REJECTED sample (resubmission) uses the same service and records isResubmission.
- Batch intake: one failing row must not commit a partial consignment unless the caller passes allowPartial=true; then failed rows are listed.

## Out of scope

- Keep existing HTTP routes and response shapes; only their internals change.
- Do not change checklist content (#156 covers configurable criteria).

## Guardrails (apply to every audit issue)

- Keep to this issue's scope. If you find a related defect, note it in the PR description instead of fixing it here.
- Never delete or overwrite analytical data, QC values or audit rows; supersede or flag instead. Migrations are additive; destructive cleanups come later (8.1).
- All status changes go through the shared contract (`server/workflowContract.js`, `transitionSample`); follow CONTRIBUTING.md §1 (scope via `utils/scopeGuard.js`, permissions via `config/roles.js`, no hard-coded labs or countries).
- Return 4xx with a stable `code` for rule violations, never 500.
- New user-facing strings: add keys in all five locales (`client/src/translations/{en,es,es-419,fr,pt}.json`, and `server/locales/` for server messages) where the surrounding code is translated.
- Existing tests must keep passing (`cd server && npm test`, `cd client && npm run build && npm run lint`), including `tests/security/wiring.test.js`.

## Done when

- Every acceptance item above is met. Items marked **[test]** have an automated test (server: `server/tests/contracts/`, run with `cd server && npm test`; client: `cd client && npm run lint` plus component or Playwright tests where noted).
- Schema changes ship as a Prisma migration under `server/prisma/migrations/` (SQLite: no Prisma enums; use shared constants plus SQL `CHECK` constraints or partial indexes where noted). Back-fills are idempotent and have a dry-run mode.
- The PR description says `Closes #<this issue>` and lists anything deferred.

**Depends on:** #180 (1.3), #181 (1.4). Start after those are merged.
